correctness.rationale: Three differential annihilator identities and complete-intersection socle degree 6 verify the apolar ideal. An explicit degree-eight reduced scheme has ideal J=(XY,Y(Y^2-Z^2),X^6+Z^4(Y^2-Z^2)); its generators lie in F^perp by the exact identity X^6+Z^4q_1=Xg+YZ^3q_2+(Z^4-XZ^3)q_1. Leading monomials XY,Y^3,X^6 give eight points, six (zeta,0,1) with zeta^6=1 and two (0,±1,1). For the lower bound, any hypothetical set of <=7 reduced apolar points extends to exactly seven. If no five collinear, cubics separate points by pairing six points into lines avoiding the seventh, degree-four relations force its vanishing ideal into (q_1,q_2), impossible because that base scheme has a doubled point. If five are collinear, the unique containing quadric is reducible q_1 or q_2. Restricting the quartic vanishing ideal to the off-line pair forces only the configuration Y=0, off-line P±, and a quintic separator then forces Z^2 to divide a squarefree binary quintic, contradiction. Direct independent symbolic differentiation and the apolar-generator inclusion identity and eight displayed zeros passed. Finite identities do not replace the universal seven-point geometry argument.
